prompt: Implement an LRU cache in Python as class LRUCache(capacity: int) with get(key) -> int (returns -1 when absent) and put(key, value) methods, both O(1), evicting the least recently used item when capacity is exceeded. get/put must refresh recency so a put on an existing key counts as a use. Provide the class; a hidden test file will import LRUCache from main.

files.test_main.py:
from main import LRUCache


def test_eviction():
    cache = LRUCache(2)
    cache.put(1, 1)
    cache.put(2, 2)
    assert cache.get(1) == 1
    cache.put(3, 3)
    assert cache.get(2) == -1
    cache.put(4, 4)
    assert cache.get(1) == -1
    assert cache.get(3) == 3
    assert cache.get(4) == 4


def test_put_refreshes_recency():
    cache = LRUCache(2)
    cache.put(1, 1)
    cache.put(2, 2)
    cache.put(1, 10)
    assert cache.get(1) == 10
    cache.put(3, 3)
    assert cache.get(2) == -1


def test_missing_returns_minus_one():
    assert LRUCache(1).get("nope") == -1

solution: An OrderedDict-based LRU: move_to_end on access, popitem(last=False) on overflow; get returns -1 for missing keys.

prompt: Explain how to detect a cycle in a singly linked list. Describe Floyd's tortoise-and-hare algorithm, prove why it terminates and detects cycles correctly, compare its space usage with a hash-set approach, and give the time complexity of each.
solution: Floyd's uses two pointers moving at speeds 1 and 2; if a cycle exists they meet; O(n) time, O(1) space, versus O(n) space for a hash set.

prompt: Compare merge sort and quicksort in terms of time complexity, space, and practical performance. Which would you choose for large in-memory lists and why?
solution: Both average O(n log n); merge sort is stable and guaranteed, but uses O(n) extra space; quicksort is in-place with better constants but O(n^2) worst case; pick based on stability/space guarantees.

prompt: Explain what a module contract is and why it matters for running generated code inside a sandboxed pipeline.
solution: A module contract fixes the exported signature, naming, and input/output format so a hidden test can import the code; breaking it fails verification even if the logic is right, which is why generated code must match it exactly in a sandboxed pipeline.
